name: Sentiment valence
definition: The degree to which expressed language is conventionally associated with positive, neutral, or negative evaluation.
claim_scope: Describes expressed evaluative language in the analyzed text.
May report positive, neutral, and negative class probabilities under a declared taxonomy.
May provide a declared normalized valence for comparison within a compatible instrument family.

expected_output.notes: Raw class probabilities must be preserved. A normalized valence is optional and must identify its transformation rule.

instrument_requirements: Declare the model taxonomy and label mapping.
Declare supported language and known training-domain limits.
Return abstained or partial status when the input falls outside supported conditions.

normalization.rule: A transformation to the interval [-1, 1] is permitted only when the exact mapping from raw labels and probabilities is versioned and preserved.

validation_requirements: Human annotation agreement under written instructions.
Tests covering mixed sentiment, quotation, negation, and irony.
Domain-shift evaluation before any domain-valid claim.

constraints: The class distribution may not be replaced by the normalized valence.
Segment variation must remain visible when an item-level summary conceals material differences.
No overall CTRT rating exists in Phase 0.

explanation_constraints: Describe language as positive, neutral, negative, mixed, or uncertain; do not describe the creator as such.
Do not infer truth, virtue, harm, intent, or audience effect.
Distinguish model probability from calibrated system confidence.
open_questions: Which normalization, if any, best preserves mixed and neutral outputs?
When is segment-level analysis mandatory rather than optional?
decision_rationale: Sentiment valence has a sufficiently bounded provisional definition and a testable output structure to enter experimental reports, while remaining ineligible for an overall rating.
